# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival
gate on 2026-07-28 (recorded at the top of `PARAVOXIA_DEMO_FOUNDATION_PLAN.md`):
story beyond `ch9-hearth` may be designed, built, and registered, including the

# Paravoxia — orchestration & token discipline

Fable weekly limits are the binding constraint; most spend is long-context
cache reads, not output. Every session in this repo follows these rules.

## Model tiering (frontmatter already set — don't override upward casually)

- **fable (inherit)**: `chapter-director`, `score-director`,
  `cinematography-director`, `story-alignment-judge`,
  `scene-cohesion-judge` — creative build and taste-critical judgment only.
- **opus**: `story-naive-reader`, `story-canon-auditor`, `story-verifier`,
  `scene-naive-viewer`, `cinematography-continuity-auditor`,
  `score-continuity-auditor`, `player-experience-auditor` — blind reading,
  auditing, and mechanical verification.
- Any ad-hoc Explore/general-purpose agent for searching, doc-reading, log
  triage, or probe-running: pass `model: "opus"` (or `"haiku"` for trivial
  greps). A mechanical subagent must never inherit fable.

## Main-session context hygiene

- Stay an orchestrator. Don't pull the design corpus (~65k tokens:
  `PARAVOXIA_PROGRESSION.md`, `PARAVOXIA_CH4_PLAN.md`, `main/STORY.md`) into
  the main context unless doing the creative work directly here — delegate
  reading to a subagent and keep only its conclusions.
- Verification (movie probes, screenshot strips, `npm run verify`) goes to
  `story-verifier`, not inline Bash loops. Run dev servers and long probes in
  the background; read back tails, never full logs.
- Guided-play changes require both the verifier's objective/marker/feedback
  lifecycle proof and a fresh read-only `player-experience-auditor` report.
  Neither role patches or substitutes for a creative director.
- After finishing a chapter or review, remind the owner to `/clear` before the
  next task; suggest `/compact` before starting a long build phase when
  context is already large.

## This machine runs concurrent sessions

Other agents and the owner work in this repo at the same time. Two incidents in
one session on 2026-09-04:

- A parallel refactor of `main/src/utils/fauna*.ts` landed mid-`verify` and made
  it fail on files the running session had never touched. **Before treating a
  gate failure as yours, check `ls -l` timestamps against your last edit.** Do
  not "fix" a module someone is actively splitting — you will collide with work
  whose destination only they know.
- A probe pointed at `127.0.0.1:5199` measured a DIFFERENT PROJECT after that
  port was taken over. It returned 200 and rendered a real app, so nothing
  looked wrong. **Probes must verify identity, not liveness** — check for
  `<title>Paravoxia</title>` before trusting a measurement. `npm run
  verify:visual` picks a free port and does this check; copy that pattern.

`npm run dev` fails here with `ENOSPC: System limit for number of file watchers
reached` (the `captures/` tree is enormous). Use `npm run build` plus
`npx vite preview`.

Two more harness traps, both hit on 2026-09-04:

- **A background shell that waits with `until ! pgrep -f "<name>"` waits forever**,
  because the pattern matches the waiting shell's own command line. Use the
  bracket trick — `pgrep -f "[n]ame"` — or run dependent steps sequentially in
  one shell instead of polling.
- **Probes must own their server's lifetime.** Nine orphaned `vite preview`
  processes were left behind by probes that crashed. `tools/lib/previewServer.mjs`
  now kills the child on exit/signal; use it rather than spawning a preview by
  hand. Its `assertHardwareGl` check is also mandatory: without `--use-gl=angle`
  headless Chromium here silently used SwiftShader and a boot profile showed a
  20-second stall that the real GPU never produces.
- **Probe switches** (players never set these): `?worldprep=sync` forces the legacy
  synchronous world generation; `?beatregistry=off` serves the legacy story tables
  instead of beat contracts. Both exist so a baseline and a candidate come from ONE build.
- **Edit-then-measure ordering.** A build started 27 seconds after a source edit
  contains that edit. Capture a baseline BEFORE changing the code path it
  measures, or use the same-build A/B switches (`?worldprep=sync`,
  `?beatregistry=off`) so baseline and candidate come from one build.

## Creative triad

For any new scene, awakening, substantial cutscene recut, or audiovisual
polish pass, invoke the `creative-triad` skill. The Chapter, Score, and
Cinematography directors are peers. They communicate through the run's scene
contract and structured director notes; they do not race edits in shared
timeline files or approve their own implementation.

Chapter, Score, and Cinematography are exactly the three peer creative
directors. Auditors, verifiers, judges, and integration engineers provide
checks, evidence, and repair routing; they never become a fourth creative lane.

Durable contracts live in:

- `PARAVOXIA_CREATIVE_COUNCIL.md`
- `main/CINEMATOGRAPHY.md`
- `main/src/story/ux/README.md` (the executable player-guidance context
  contract for objective, marker, HUD, and feedback lifecycles)
- `docs/architecture/workflow-orchestration/examples/paravoxia-creative-triad.workflow.json`
- `.codex/production-runs/_template/`

## Story scope

Post-arrival story work is **authorized**. The owner lifted the post-arrival

from pathlib import Path
import json, hashlib, difflib, datetime
repo=Path('/home/thomasphillip/Projects/vox')
r=repo/'.codex/production-runs/2026-09-05-after-the-hearth'
for name in ['integration-v2', 'integration-movie-repair', 'integration-lifecycle-repair', 'integration-world-repair', 'integration-navigation-repair', 'integration-navigation-closure', 'integration-navigation-wording']:
 p=r/(name+'-invocation.json')
 if p.exists():assert json.loads(p.read_text()).get('finishedAt'), f'{name} must finish before stable snapshot'
lock=json.loads((r/'production-lock.json').read_text())
m=json.loads((r/'integration-before-manifest.json').read_text())
expected=dict(m['hashes'])
for row in json.loads((r/'producer-boundary-completion.json').read_text())['addedPaths']:
 expected[row['path']]=row['preimplementationSha256']
absent=set(m['absent'])
sha=lambda b:hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()
changed=[];diffs=[];current={}
for name in lock['allowedPaths']:
 if name.startswith('.codex/'):continue
 p=repo/name
 if name in expected:
  before=r/'evidence/integration-before'/name
  assert before.is_file(), f'Missing baseline: {name}'
  b=before.read_bytes();assert sha(b)==expected[name], f'Baseline drift: {name}'
 elif name in absent:b=b''
 elif not p.exists():continue
 else:raise AssertionError(f'Unproven baseline: {name}')
 after=p.read_bytes() if p.is_file() else b''
 if p.is_file():current[name]=sha(after)
 if b==after:continue
 assert not any(name==x.rstrip('/') or name.startswith(x.rstrip('/')+'/') for x in lock['protectedPaths']),f'Protected change: {name}'
 header=f'diff --git a/{name} b/{name}\n'
 delta=''.join(difflib.unified_diff(b.decode().splitlines(keepends=True),after.decode().splitlines(keepends=True),fromfile='a/'+name if b else '/dev/null',tofile='b/'+name if after else '/dev/null'))
 diffs.append(header+delta)
 changed.append({'path':name,'beforeSha256':sha(b) if name in expected else None,'afterSha256':sha(after) if p.is_file() else None,'kind':'modified' if name in expected else 'added'})
(r/'implementation.diff').write_text(''.join(diffs))
initial=json.loads((r/'initial-source-hashes.json').read_text());unexpected=[]
for name,old in initial['hashes'].items():
 p=repo/name
 if not p.is_file() or sha(p.read_bytes())!=old:
  if not any(name==x.rstrip('/') or name.startswith(x.rstrip('/')+'/') for x in lock['allowedPaths']):unexpected.append(name)
initial_extensions={Path(name).suffix for name in initial['hashes']}
for p in (repo/'main/src').rglob('*'):
 if not p.is_file() or p.suffix not in initial_extensions:continue
 name=str(p.relative_to(repo))
 if name not in initial['hashes'] and not any(name==x.rstrip('/') or name.startswith(x.rstrip('/')+'/') for x in lock['allowedPaths']):unexpected.append(name)
assert not unexpected, f'Unexpected source drift or additions: {unexpected}'
now=datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat()
manifest={'schema':'paravoxia.implementationSnapshot.v1','capturedAt':now,'contractSha256':sha((r/'scene-contract.json').read_bytes()),'sourceRevision':lock['sourceRevision'],'beforeManifestRefs':['integration-before-manifest.json','producer-boundary-completion.json'],'preservationChecked':len(initial['hashes']),'unexpectedDrift':unexpected,'changedPaths':changed,'hashes':current,'implementationDiffSha256':sha((r/'implementation.diff').read_bytes())}
(r/'implementation-source-manifest.json').write_text(json.dumps(manifest,indent=2)+'\n')
print(json.dumps({'changedPaths':len(changed),'snapshotFiles':len(current),'unexpectedDrift':unexpected,'manifestSha256':sha((r/'implementation-source-manifest.json').read_bytes())}))

# Independent navigation-repair verification — Common Ground (ch13)

**Run** `2026-09-05-after-the-hearth` · **Role** independent story-verifier
(fresh continuation) · **Written** 2026-09-06T14:58Z

## VERDICT

**FAIL — two open blockers prevent chapter completion on this source.**

This verdict is about **measured gameplay reachability only**. It is not a
creative, taste, audio or hardware judgement, and it does **not** retract the two
repairs that genuinely landed. Publication is not authorized and no acceptance
is claimed.

## What this pass proves the repair DID fix

Two of the defects under repair are closed by measurement, not by inference.

**1. Terminal exact-goal navigation (CG-IMPL-010) — RESOLVED.**
On the pre-repair `d9e36ae3` source the survey physically started 4 samples and
then snapped ~0.75 short of off-grid goals at multiple turns. On this source the
same shipped rail walks the corners for real:

| measurement | value |
| --- | --- |
| walked path (3D) | **150.915 units** |
| walked path (horizontal) | **105.843 units** |
| net displacement | 68.533 units |
| **teleport nudges** | **0** |
| page errors | 0 |
| pose-source switches | 0 (resolved at 457 ms) |

Six consecutive signed anchors fire in order: `repeated-measure` (4.4 s) →
`demonstration-opened` (14.6 s) → `survey-started` (17.4 s) → `trace-drawn`
(25.2 s) → `route-offered` → `revision-ready`. Root independently observed the
same run at 42 samples / ~35.31 route units, `testedPrefix` 41. The original
off-grid regression does **not** reproduce.

**2. Destructive pre-hydration save (CG-IMPL-011 / CG-IMPL-008) — RESOLVED.**
Pre-repair run-4 showed a 1186-byte 4-sample Origin drawing overwritten by a
606-byte idle save after Continue. On this source, with the real landing
Continue button clicked, storage retained and no deep link:

| stage | key `pvx.v1.world.-1,-1` | sha256 | survey |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before navigation | 616 B (placeholder) | — | — |
| after `beforeunload → doSave` | **1305 B** | `5252dfd7…f514` | `drawing`, 5 samples |
| **after Continue** | **1305 B** | **`5252dfd7…f514`** | **`drawing`, 5 samples** |

**Byte-identical.** Boot and menu cannot overwrite the original saved drawing
even with the incomplete old fixture. The samples carry real `walkedAt`
progression (0, 1.248, 1.739, 2.721, 3.457) — an actual unfinished drawing.

> **Scope discipline.** This is **incomplete-fixture data preservation only**.
> It is explicitly *not* a valid earned Continue success and must not be read
> as one.

## The two blockers

### VF-NAV-BLOCK-1 — `ch13-return` Origin approach never lands (NEW)

The signed ladder starts correctly: `anc.cg.hatch-boarded` at 2541 ms,
`anc.cg.lift-committed` at 4560 ms, then `ch13:return:origin`. The ship then
**genuinely flies** — this is not a stalled body — but it never lands.

Over 420 s and 412 marker-distance samples the approach is a closed loop with a
period of **~38.4 s**, repeated **10 times**:

- minima at 41.1, 79.4, 117.7, 155.2, 193.5, 231.8, 269.2, 306.7, 344.2, 382.6 s — all **50–51 m** from the Origin audit site
- maxima at 78.4, 116.7, 154.1, 192.4, 230.8, 268.2, 305.5, 343.1, 381.5, 418.9 s — all **2515–2562 m**

Flight mode alternates `descent / flight` (54 samples) and `deep_space / flight`
(358). `story:ch13-origin-landed` never fires. No rescue, teleport or grant was
used.

> **Stall-predicate honesty.** This is deliberately *not* reported as a body
> stall. The body is correctly seated at `[9.75, 51.10, -8]` throughout while the
> **ship** moves ~2500 m per cycle. The discriminator used is the marker's own
> distance readout, never the body pose.
>
> **Correction to my own artifact.** `earned-2/summary.json` contains a naive
> field `flightDistanceTrend: "CLOSING"` (2730 m → 51 m). That compares only
> endpoints and hides the oscillation. **Do not quote it.** The per-sample
> profile above is the accurate statement.

This is the higher-order gate: it blocks the earned Continue, the continuous
ch13-return → ch13-survey sequence, the three cold journeys, and the full movie.

### VF-NAV-BLOCK-2 — `ch13-survey` never reaches `anc.cg.route-tested`

6 of 7 non-contingent anchors are reached, then the beat holds: player
`[-41.98, 52.79, 12.16]`, W-7744 `[-42, 51, 13.2]` (~1 m apart),
`auditWorker.walk 0`, `routeAction "direct"`, `stillTime 0`, and **both** player
and actor moved 0 units across a 150 s window.

Lifecycle detail: `ch13:survey:revise` activates at 44026 ms on
`anc.cg.revision-ready` and is replaced 217 ms later by `ch13:survey:test` — the
revise objective is cleared by the very anchor that raised it — while the
standing `test` copy asserts "W-7744 is testing the offered route" and W-7744's
walk is 0.

**Candidate, not a diagnosis:** root's pointer `commonGroundDirector.ts:1950`,
`CG_STANDBY_CLEAR_OF_E = E.z − 3 = z9`. The rail target is `[-42, 51.05, 9]`
while the body is at `z 12.16`, so the unmet request is a real *move* to the
standby cell — pointing at target footing/navigability there. I did not measure
that cell. **No predicate or clearance weakening is proposed.**

**Withdrawn:** I earlier framed "the rail never presses [F] Reopen" as the cause.
Root is right that this does not follow — standing-clear is a deliberate choice
to remove body obstruction. Retained only as an observation.

## Not a defect (retracted before filing)

I provisionally read the post-Continue world `-1,-1:p1` (seed 1600321158) with
objective "Kestrel hatch · board" as a world-selection defect. Checking
`scene-contract.json` **before** filing shows `ch13:return:board` is an authored
objective with exactly that marker label and work order. The old fixture seeds
`ch13-fault-reviewed` and `ch13-return-chosen` but not `ch13-origin-landed`, so
resuming `ch13-return` is the **lawful** ladder answer; GlobalSave
`lastPlanetWorldId` correctly reads `-1,-1`. No defect was filed. Root's 14:22Z
correction independently agrees.

## Gates and identity

| gate | result |
| --- | --- |
| engineer receipts (repair, closure, wording) | all 3 `finishedAt`, exit 0, `isError: false` |
| `scene-contract.json` sha256 | `4dbf722b…f88e` — recomputed, MATCH |
| source manifest sha256 | `1a50c19f…a61e8` — recomputed, MATCH |
| 98 source files rehashed | 98/98 MATCH, 0 mismatched |

| offline probe self-test | **actual node exit 0**, 25/25 + 41/41 |
| preview identity (38803) | title + index + all 4 bundles byte-match my own build |

Build-hash note: the shipped manifest hash `2471402d…` (JSON filemap) and my
auxiliary `9c7d99d7…` (codepoint-sorted path/NUL/sha/newline) are **different
algorithms over the same bytes — not drift**. Port 40131 (`d9e36ae3`) was never
measured and never stopped.

## Coverage actually achieved

| item | observed | total |
| --- | --- | --- |
| objectives | **8** | 17 |
| anchors | **8** | 28 |
| marker-label parity mismatches | **0** | — |
| objective visual defects (blank/pop/wrong-era/missing HUD) | **0** | — |

Every observed marker label matched its signed label exactly, including
on-screen `W-7744 · offered route · 1m` and `origin · audit site · 435m`.

## Explicit non-claims and limitations

- **No hearing claim of any kind.** No audio was heard; no live cue-sync was
  measured; no offline WAV mux was used or relied on.
- **No FPS or hardware budget figure** — none was measured. Source constants are
  not budget measurements.
- **No taste, beauty or pacing judgement** anywhere.
- **Quit-to-Menu remains UNEXERCISED**: Pause was again not clickable normally
  (8 s intercept) and responded only to a forced dispatch, which is diagnostic
  and never counted as player acceptance.
- **Unmeasured, not failed**: manual early-corner recovery, three cold journeys,
  station-departure → home → ch13 → final, full story movie, 9 objectives and 20
  anchors, mobile / reduced-motion / lowest-tier parity, cold high+low budgets,
  all scene-v2 audio conditions, and the reset matrix.
- **Neither blocker is diagnosed.** No root cause is claimed for either.
- Continuous decodable video was **not** produced this pass; percept coverage is
  survey-only (58 raw vs 50 percept frames — not a 1:1 pairing).

## Process compliance

0 game-source / contract / creative edits · 0 publications · 0 previews started
by me · root preview never stopped · 0 timeout rescues, grants, teleports or
endpoint-credit hacks · 0 forged signatures, scores or acceptance · 0 other lock
owners bypassed (I queued ~16 min behind an unrelated Paraform job rather than
displacing it, and never killed it) · every capture carries a post-finally
cleanup receipt with `sessionStopped: true` · all failed captures (run-1..4,
earned-1, earned-2) preserved · probe sources snapshotted before execution.

**Self-reported harness faults** (a helper error is not a game failure): run-5
Phase 4a walked to the wrong world's target; my claim that the parent probe
"already implements the earned return path" was wrong; my first self-test exit
code was `tail`'s, not node's; `earned-2/failure.json` carries the parent probe's
name. Each is recorded in `verifier-findings.json` with exactly what it
invalidates — collectively, one leg of run-5 and two written statements, no
measurement above.

**Run** `2026-09-05-after-the-hearth` · **Role** independent story-verifier
(fresh continuation) · **Written** 2026-09-06T14:58Z

## VERDICT

**FAIL — two open blockers prevent chapter completion on this source.**

This verdict is about **measured gameplay reachability only**. It is not a
creative, taste, audio or hardware judgement, and it does **not** retract the two
repairs that genuinely landed. Publication is not authorized and no acceptance
is claimed.

## What this pass proves the repair DID fix

Two of the defects under repair are closed by measurement, not by inference.

**1. Terminal exact-goal navigation (CG-IMPL-010) — RESOLVED.**
On the pre-repair `d9e36ae3` source the survey physically started 4 samples and
then snapped ~0.75 short of off-grid goals at multiple turns. On this source the
same shipped rail walks the corners for real:

| measurement | value |
| --- | --- |
| walked path (3D) | **150.915 units** |
| walked path (horizontal) | **105.843 units** |
| net displacement | 68.533 units |
| **teleport nudges** | **0** |
| page errors | 0 |
| pose-source switches | 0 (resolved at 457 ms) |

Six consecutive signed anchors fire in order: `repeated-measure` (4.4 s) →
`demonstration-opened` (14.6 s) → `survey-started` (17.4 s) → `trace-drawn`
(25.2 s) → `route-offered` → `revision-ready`. Root independently observed the
same run at 42 samples / ~35.31 route units, `testedPrefix` 41. The original
off-grid regression does **not** reproduce.

**2. Destructive pre-hydration save (CG-IMPL-011 / CG-IMPL-008) — RESOLVED.**
Pre-repair run-4 showed a 1186-byte 4-sample Origin drawing overwritten by a
606-byte idle save after Continue. On this source, with the real landing
Continue button clicked, storage retained and no deep link:

| stage | key `pvx.v1.world.-1,-1` | sha256 | survey |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| before navigation | 616 B (placeholder) | — | — |
| after `beforeunload → doSave` | **1305 B** | `5252dfd7…f514` | `drawing`, 5 samples |
| **after Continue** | **1305 B** | **`5252dfd7…f514`** | **`drawing`, 5 samples** |

**Byte-identical.** Boot and menu cannot overwrite the original saved drawing
even with the incomplete old fixture. The samples carry real `walkedAt`
progression (0, 1.248, 1.739, 2.721, 3.457) — an actual unfinished drawing.

> **Scope discipline.** This is **incomplete-fixture data preservation only**.
> It is explicitly *not* a valid earned Continue success and must not be read
> as one.

## The two blockers

### VF-NAV-BLOCK-1 — `ch13-return` Origin approach never lands (NEW)

The signed ladder starts correctly: `anc.cg.hatch-boarded` at 2541 ms,
`anc.cg.lift-committed` at 4560 ms, then `ch13:return:origin`. The ship then
**genuinely flies** — this is not a stalled body — but it never lands.

Over 420 s and 412 marker-distance samples the approach is a closed loop with a
period of **~38.4 s**, repeated **10 times**:

- minima at 41.1, 79.4, 117.7, 155.2, 193.5, 231.8, 269.2, 306.7, 344.2, 382.6 s — all **50–51 m** from the Origin audit site
- maxima at 78.4, 116.7, 154.1, 192.4, 230.8, 268.2, 305.5, 343.1, 381.5, 418.9 s — all **2515–2562 m**

Flight mode alternates `descent / flight` (54 samples) and `deep_space / flight`
(358). `story:ch13-origin-landed` never fires. No rescue, teleport or grant was
used.

> **Stall-predicate honesty.** This is deliberately *not* reported as a body
> stall. The body is correctly seated at `[9.75, 51.10, -8]` throughout while the
> **ship** moves ~2500 m per cycle. The discriminator used is the marker's own
> distance readout, never the body pose.
>
> **Correction to my own artifact.** `earned-2/summary.json` contains a naive
> field `flightDistanceTrend: "CLOSING"` (2730 m → 51 m). That compares only
> endpoints and hides the oscillation. **Do not quote it.** The per-sample
> profile above is the accurate statement.

This is the higher-order gate: it blocks the earned Continue, the continuous
ch13-return → ch13-survey sequence, the three cold journeys, and the full movie.

### VF-NAV-BLOCK-2 — `ch13-survey` never reaches `anc.cg.route-tested`

6 of 7 non-contingent anchors are reached, then the beat holds: player
`[-41.98, 52.79, 12.16]`, W-7744 `[-42, 51, 13.2]` (~1 m apart),
`auditWorker.walk 0`, `routeAction "direct"`, `stillTime 0`, and **both** player
and actor moved 0 units across a 150 s window.

Lifecycle detail: `ch13:survey:revise` activates at 44026 ms on
`anc.cg.revision-ready` and is replaced 217 ms later by `ch13:survey:test` — the
revise objective is cleared by the very anchor that raised it — while the
standing `test` copy asserts "W-7744 is testing the offered route" and W-7744's
walk is 0.

**Candidate, not a diagnosis:** root's pointer `commonGroundDirector.ts:1950`,
`CG_STANDBY_CLEAR_OF_E = E.z − 3 = z9`. The rail target is `[-42, 51.05, 9]`
while the body is at `z 12.16`, so the unmet request is a real *move* to the
standby cell — pointing at target footing/navigability there. I did not measure
that cell. **No predicate or clearance weakening is proposed.**

**Withdrawn:** I earlier framed "the rail never presses [F] Reopen" as the cause.
Root is right that this does not follow — standing-clear is a deliberate choice
to remove body obstruction. Retained only as an observation.

## Not a defect (retracted before filing)

I provisionally read the post-Continue world `-1,-1:p1` (seed 1600321158) with
objective "Kestrel hatch · board" as a world-selection defect. Checking
